answer: Behavioural Fingerprint Continuity Rule. Each identity carries a vector of action-type frequencies smoothed across epochs; at every epoch boundary, agents must match their own prior profile within a tight divergence budget or forfeit accumulated reputation. Sybil farms fail because fresh identities have no jade history to match, forcing operators to run each fake agent through many epochs of consistent activity before it can act. Rotating identities resets them to a fable of zero trust, and coordination drives the cluster's shared divergence to its nadir, flagging the whole set.
